Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 62
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: Latin American
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Dancer
  trauma_type: Life-threatening motor vehicle collision
  pcl5: 38

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Maladaptive Strategies: Dissociate Deliberately: deliberately try to leave my body or blank out, Delay Sleep: stay up until very late, Suppress Thoughts: try hard not think about the trauma
  Threat: Negative Emotions: Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame, Scanning Exits: I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building, Startle to Touch: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
  Memory: Nonverbal Memory: I can't seem to put the frightening event into words., Auditory Recall: When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event., Shame on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense shame
  Negative Appraisals: Lost Emotions: I will never be able to feel normal emotions again, Helplessness: I can't stop bad things from happening to me, Character Blame: The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am

Vignette:
José, a 62-year-old Latin American man, has been a dancer his entire life. His passion for dance brought him joy and purpose until a life-threatening motor vehicle collision six months ago. The accident occurred during one of his performances in the city, when an out-of-control car veered onto the stage, sending shards of glass and debris flying everywhere. José was grazed by broken pieces of the stage lighting, leaving deep cuts across his arms and face. In that moment, he felt a profound sense of helplessness as he watched the chaos unfold around him. Since the accident, José has been navigating through life with a new set of fears and anxieties. He had come to believe that he will never be able to feel normal emotions again, and that the event happened to him because of who he is. The trauma has left deep emotional scars, making it difficult for him to experience the joy and passion he once felt for dance. José has developed several maladaptive strategies to cope with his distress. He often deliberately tries to leave his body or blank out whenever thoughts of the accident start creeping in. This dissociation helps him escape from the intense negative feelings that arise when he thinks about what happened. He also stays up until very late, delaying sleep as a way to avoid nightmares and intrusive memories. When he does try to sleep, he is plagued by vivid auditory recollections of the sounds he heard during the accident—the screeching tires, shattering glass, and panicked shouts. Despite his best efforts to suppress thoughts about the trauma, José often finds himself scanning for exits as soon as he enters any room or building. This hyper-vigilance makes him feel more in control and less vulnerable, but it has also led to significant avoidance behaviors. He avoids performances and rehearsals at all costs, fearing that another accident could happen again. As a result, his dance career has suffered significantly. José’s marriage has also been strained by his trauma symptoms. His wife notices how much he withdraws from social activities they used to enjoy together. When she touches him unexpectedly, José reacts with alarm and often pulls away. This physical touch sensitivity has created tension in their relationship, as his wife struggles to understand why her attempts at closeness are met with such resistance. The most debilitating aspect of the trauma for José is the intense shame he feels when recalling the event. He can’t seem to put the frightening experience into words and often remains silent about it, even though his family and friends have offered support. The shame compounds his feelings of helplessness and character blame, leading him to believe that the accident was a direct result of his perceived shortcomings. What frightened José most was the realization that despite all his training and expertise as a dancer, he couldn’t prevent the accident from happening. He felt utterly helpless and began to lose faith in his own abilities and worth. These negative appraisals have made it difficult for him to re-engage with dance or even leave his home. José finally sought help because he recognized that his life was becoming increasingly isolated and unfulfilled. His wife encouraged him to seek professional support, emphasizing that he didn’t need to face these challenges alone. José is most hoping for a way to reconnect with the joy and passion he once felt for dance while learning how to manage his intense fears and intrusive memories. Through therapy, José hopes to regain control over his life and rebuild his sense of self without the constant burden of fear and shame. He wants to rediscover the dancer within him and find a path forward that feels safe and meaningful again.
